QUESTIONS\u003Cdiv\u003E1. \u003Cb\u003EThe sensitivity of diagnosing BPH or prostatomegaly by ultrasound?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBPH appears in TRUS as an echogenic and non-mobile mass. TRUS is mainly used to assess prostate volume, which is crucial for therapeutic strategies. Prostate volume can be estimated by serial planimetry, orthogonal plane, rotational body (single plane, ellipsoid) and three-dimensional methods.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStaging sensitivities in studies using grey-scale TRUS varied between 30% and 50% with specificities between 77% and 96%. Three-dimensional TRUS aided in the assessment of extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle invasion.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. \u003Cb\u003ECauses of muscle atrophy in the leg since childhood ?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eremaining immobile for long periods due to illness or injury\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eage\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emalnutrition\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Egenetics\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eneurological problems\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ecertain medical conditions, such as arthritis, myositis, ALS, and MS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. \u003Cb\u003EMuscles responsible for abduction and adduction of foot?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAbduction:- Abductor Hallucis belongs to the superficial layer of the plantar foot muscles, alongside the Flexor Digitorum Brevis and Abductor Digiti Minimi.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdduction:-Adductor hallucis muscle\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELEARNING POINTS:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1.How to correlate history with the cause of disease?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.what is the importantance of daily routine approach?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3.Causes of decreased urine output\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4. best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is retired accountant came to the OPD with\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINTS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Edecreased urine output since 1 day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShortness of breath since 1 day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 1day ago when he developed decreased urine output which was sudden in onset, associated with urgency and pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe has shortness of breath since 1 day which is sudden in onset gradually progressive aggravated on walking and relieved by taking rest.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of abdominal distention and facial puffiness on and off since 3 months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of fever, chest pain, palpitations, cough and back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKnown case of hypothyroidism since 1 yr\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of diabetes mellitus, epilepsy, asthma .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETREATMENT HISTORY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ET.Ramipril and metoprolol for hypertension\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ET. Thyronorm for hypothyroidism\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPercutaneous Coronary Intervention stenting was done for CAD.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of haemorrhoidectomy 8 years
